hints: Build a cumulative frequency table by computing running totals of the shopper frequencies across each class interval.
Plot each cumulative frequency at the upper boundary of its interval: $(30, 16)$, $(50, 56)$, $(70, 104)$, $(90, 130)$, $(140, 160)$, starting at $(0, 0)$.
Use uniform linear scales: horizontal axis covering at least $0$ to $140$ dollars and vertical axis covering $0$ to $160$ cumulative frequency.
Connect the plotted points with a smooth curve or polygon through $(0, 0)$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the cumulative frequencies by adding each group's frequency to the running total:
$$\begin{aligned} t \le 30: & \quad 16 \\ t \le 50: & \quad 16 + 40 = 56 \\ t \le 70: & \quad 56 + 48 = 104 \\ t \le 90: & \quad 104 + 26 = 130 \\ t \le 140: & \quad 130 + 30 = 160 \end{aligned}$$
Plot each cumulative frequency against the upper boundary of its class interval: $(0,0), (30,16), (50,56), (70,104), (90,130), (140,160)$.
Join the plotted points with a smooth, continuous cumulative frequency curve.

hints: For total frequency $N = 160$, locate the median at cumulative frequency $0.5 \times 160 = 80$, the lower quartile $Q_1$ at $0.25 \times 160 = 40$, and the upper quartile $Q_3$ at $0.75 \times 160 = 120$.
Read horizontally from these cumulative frequencies to the curve, then vertically down to read the corresponding amounts on the spending axis.
Calculate the interquartile range using $\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
walkthrough: The median corresponds to half of the total 160 shoppers ($160 / 2 = 80$). Locate 80 on the vertical cumulative frequency axis and read across to the curve: the median is $\$59$.
The lower quartile ($Q_1$) is at a cumulative frequency of $160 / 4 = 40$. Reading across to the curve gives $Q_1 = \$43$.
The upper quartile ($Q_3$) is at a cumulative frequency of $3 \times 40 = 120$. Reading across to the curve gives $Q_3 = \$82$.

Subtract the lower quartile from the upper quartile to calculate the interquartile range:
$$\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 82 - 43 = 39\text{ dollars}$$

hints: Locate $\$115$ on the horizontal axis and read up to the cumulative frequency curve to determine how many shoppers spent $\$115$ or less.
Subtract that cumulative frequency reading from the total of $160$ shoppers to find how many spent more than $\$115$.
walkthrough: Locate $\$115$ on the horizontal amount-spent axis and read up to the cumulative frequency curve: the cumulative frequency is 149 shoppers.

Subtract from the total of 160 shoppers to find how many spent more than $\$115$:
$$\text{Shoppers spending } > \$115 = 160 - 149 = 11\text{ shoppers}$$

hints: Estimate the mean of grouped continuous data using the midpoint of each class interval.
Compute the midpoints $x$ of the 5 intervals: $15$, $40$, $60$, $80$, and $115$.
Multiply each midpoint by its frequency, sum the products $\sum fx$, and divide by total frequency $160$.
walkthrough:
Find the midpoint of each price interval by averaging its lower and upper boundaries:
$$\text{Midpoints: } 15, 40, 60, 80, 115$$

Multiply each midpoint by the number of shoppers in that group, and sum them to get the total amount spent:
$$\sum fx = (15 \times 16) + (40 \times 40) + (60 \times 48) + (80 \times 26) + (115 \times 30) = 240 + 1600 + 2880 + 2080 + 3450 = 10250$$

Divide by the total of 160 shoppers to estimate the mean:
$$\text{Mean} = \frac{10250}{160} = 64.0625 \approx 64.1\text{ dollars}$$
